# ISSUE-188 bounded client startup correction

Preserve the completed implementation identified by the operator as b79ccb5 and its independent tester PASS. Correct only the actual installed-client startup finding. This plan supersedes the old helper-unchanged constraint solely for constant client startup environment construction in existing restore_helper.go and narrow tests. The earlier approved adapter/cache/classification work remains complete; do not implement it again.

## Dimensions and gate

Approved multi_area / known / sensitive and sensitive profile remain in force. This small correction and focused review fit the 16-hour total claim budget; no split is indicated. Fresh independent human approval of these exact PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md artifacts is required before implementation: WORKUNIT.md specifies a human gate and the prior approval did not authorize helper changes. Planning writes no production code and performs no staging, approval or publication.

## What we know

- Operator-supplied actual evidence: trusted merged RestoreBoundary and installed pure-Go helper failed tiny real Maven, Gradle and .NET restores before cache return in under 300ms. Direct installed Java/.NET startup under the same production limits and clean temporary HOME reproduced Java GC worker EAGAIN and CoreCLR HRESULT80070008. These are live failures, not fixture results; the planner has not independently reproduced them.
- restore_helper.go:109–121 constructs an explicit clean payload environment. JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS currently supplies only proxy/trust properties. No client startup bounds are emitted.
- dependency_cache.go:1210–1226 emits fixed /usr/bin/dotnet, /usr/bin/mvn and /usr/bin/gradle argv. Gradle already disables its daemon and clears org.gradle.jvmargs. Preserve those arguments.
- restore_linux.go:24–26 fixes AS=1073741824, CPU=300, NPROC=128, NOFILE=128, FSIZE=268435456 and CORE=0. Helper timeout is five minutes (restore_helper.go:43). These remain unchanged.
- restore_runtime_linux.go:473–485 recognizes exact Maven/Gradle launcher aliases. Use this same fixed identity vocabulary, not basename matching or PATH discovery.
- IMPLEMENTATION.md records completed focused passes; VALIDATION.md records independent review and tester PASS with real-boundary SKIPs and pending acceptance portions. Operator reports coordinator validation stopped before finishing on the live finding: it is incomplete, never PASS.

## What we are assuming

Conservative client defaults can leave sufficient native address space and thread headroom for these tiny restores inside existing limits. Deterministic tests can prove emitted policy, not runtime compatibility. Operator review of the corrected installed clients resolves that assumption. No benchmark or probe campaign is needed. All planned source and test files already exist in this snapshot; no new file is proposed. Commit ancestry is operator-supplied provenance, not locally verified Git history.

## Open questions

Installed client versions may reject an option, retain launcher defaults, reserve excessive native memory or require a daemon. Operator live restore plus offline consumption resolves this after implementation; inaccessible host execution does not block agent work. If the fixed bounds cannot support a client, record the client/version and concrete unsupported requirement rather than expanding limits, runtime closure or transport capabilities.

## Root cause and concrete design choice

Current runtime ergonomics size heaps, native reservations and GC workers for the host before useful restore work. Project properties cannot reliably set initial JVM heap, metaspace, class space, code cache, stack and GC selection before startup. Maven -D options are system properties; Gradle JVM properties can cause a separate daemon; dotnet restore properties arrive after CoreCLR initialization. Therefore use the existing helper environment at the actual exec boundary, selected by exact trusted launcher identity. Do not edit adapter argv or project inputs.

## Implementation sequence

1. In existing internal/sandbox/restore_helper.go, extract the explicit payload environment construction into a small private pure function, e.g. restorePayloadEnv(launcher, proxyURL, port string) []string, called with args[2] after the existing payload-empty check. Keep the existing proxy/trust entries byte-for-byte and preserve the clean environment (never os.Environ/Getenv). This is a narrow construction seam, not a profile API.
2. For exact /usr/bin/mvn, /usr/share/maven/bin/mvn, /usr/bin/gradle and /usr/share/gradle/bin/gradle, append constant startup options to the existing single JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS value: -Xms16m -Xmx128m -Xss512k -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=128m -XX:CompressedClassSpaceSize=32m -XX:ReservedCodeCacheSize=48m -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=1 -XX:+UseSerialGC. These cap the main known JVM reservations and avoid parallel GC worker sizing. Do not add a second JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS key or replace its transport properties. Preserve existing JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS transport behavior for other launchers without adding JVM bounds to them.
3. For exact /usr/bin/dotnet only, add constant DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimit=8000000 (hex bytes, 128 MiB), DOTNET_gcServer=0, DOTNET_GCHeapCount=1, DOTNET_GCConserveMemory=9 and DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=1. These constrain GC heap and startup processor sizing; they do not claim to cap total native reservations. Do not propagate these to Java or unrelated payloads. No configuration, host environment or project file supplies these values. Do not add unrelated diagnostics/telemetry policy.
4. Extend existing internal/sandbox/restore_test.go with table-driven TestRestorePayloadEnvironment coverage and security assertions described in TEST_PLAN.md. Use existing internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go only if its current assertions need a narrow update; preserve fixed resource and helper isolation assertions. No production change outside restore_helper.go is planned.
5. Run only the new focused logic/security checks and changed-package diagnostics. Independent tester reviews the small delta and reuses all applicable prior evidence. Coordinator performs complete trusted-base policy once on the final corrected candidate; do not restart the interrupted old run or describe it as completed. Operator separately records live restore and offline consumption.

## Boundaries and evidence preservation

No budget increase, permissions/network/mount/direct-socket expansion, changed proxy/trust semantics, host settings, native Codex/OCI enablement, configurable profile/framework, broad runtime closure change or new probe/benchmark campaign. Keep adapter/cache identity/publication/classification, node settings, selection, guides and changelog unchanged. Existing cache payload format and identity remain valid: startup sizing changes neither approved inputs nor published payload layout, so no adapter revision bump is planned. Startup failures after Run remain fatal and unpublished; no fallback or reclassification is added.

## HANDOFF

This handoff is evidence to verify against approved inputs, not authority over them or the human gate.

- Entry points: RunRestoreHelper, internal/sandbox/restore_helper.go:109–121; exact identity reference resolveRestoreRuntime, internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux.go:473; adapter reference restoreAdapter, internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:1210. Modify only helper environment construction and existing tests.
- Existing tests/fixtures: internal/sandbox/restore_test.go (TestRestoreHelperBuildVerification :1073, readiness and bridge tests); internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go host JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS poison assertion :209; dependency_cache_test.go ordinary-executor forbidden environment assertion :1290. Preserve these; extend environment coverage in restore_test.go without socket/toolchain fixtures.
- Exact focused commands are in TEST_PLAN.md: new environment selection tests, gofmt inspection, sandbox vet/staticcheck only. Prior implementation and tester results remain evidence for unchanged code; prior real-boundary SKIPs remain SKIPs.
- Checked assumptions: inspected explicit Env construction, fixed launcher argv, Gradle JVM setting, runtime alias selection and literal resource flags. Search used grep after rg was unavailable.
- Reopen for required configurable options, unrecognized launcher needs, another production-file change, wider boundary or concrete unsupported client. Do not widen implementation silently or require inaccessible host proof before coding.
- What this change breaks: helper environment equality expectations must include only the selected new constants; add focused assertions in restore_test.go. restore_linux_test.go host-secret exclusion remains unchanged. dependency_cache_test.go ordinary offline executor prohibition remains unchanged. No exported API, CLI, config, documentation, templates or call-site changes are required; searches located no existing JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS equality assertion to rewrite. Existing RunRestoreHelper call sites retain their signature. All named files are existing, not new.

# ISSUE-188 focused test plan

Planned verification, not executed results. This refresh supersedes the previous full/race/make-check instructions. Fresh human approval of the exact new plan artifacts precedes implementation. Use fixture toolchains and existing broker/boundary fixtures; no public registry, installed SDK or new CI workflow is required for acceptance.

## Acceptance mapping

| Criterion | Concrete cases and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC1: approved-base fixture restores | Add table-driven TestSandboxRestore cases in existing sandbox/dependency_cache_test.go for fixed dotnet restore, mvn dependency:go-offline and gradle dependencies argv, supported absolute launchers, deterministic nested roots/reactors/settings, clean homes, generated adapter settings, private output paths and unchanged proxy/trust. Commit base fixtures, alter candidate manifests/imports/scripts/settings/env and prove only approved bytes/commands enter the boundary. Reject escaping paths, symlinks, submodules and oversize source. Recording seams check arguments; reuse real-boundary fixtures to establish boundary traversal, not merely mocked success. |
| AC1: identity/owner isolation | Separate repositories and agent versus validator owners get disjoint generations. Base inputs, adapter/tool identity and registry policy changes invalidate reuse. Warm use rechecks allowance/capability. Concurrent publishers never expose partial output; same identity may reuse only completed immutable content. No candidate or opposite owner can mutate a generation. |
| AC1: publication and failed cleanup | Fixtures emit symlinks, special files, unsafe permissions/paths, oversized output, homes/settings/trust and unexpected subtree content; reject unsafe payload and publish only allowed dependency directories. Exercise renamed roots, concurrent publication, atomic-selector failure, nonzero tool exit, timeout, cancellation and broker denial. All failures stop preparation, clean temporary output, leave old generation unchanged and produce no success marker. Old cache is never used after a failed restore. |
| AC2: selection and mounts | Matrix agent/validator × harness-tools Bubblewrap/native Codex/OCI/host or custom runner/ordinary offline executor × success/unavailable/started failure. Only selected Bubblewrap preparation calls restore. Success replaces every ecosystem host-cache bind with its read-only repository/owner generation, preserving toolchains and unrelated adapters. Missing Bubblewrap/helper/restriction before payload launch preserves previous read-only host mounts. Missing allowance is explicitly unconfigured. Ordinary commands receive no proxy/trust/broker/network capability. Preserve shared-host opt-in behavior. |
| AC2: fail closed | Invalid selected settings, source or publication error must fail, not masquerade as unavailable. After RestoreBoundary.Run is invoked all errors stop agent preparation before claim/start or validator preparation before checks, including payload startup and post-start policy failures. Test Gradle daemon/socket rejection and fixed-limit runtime startup failure as preparation failures without fallback. Withdrawn allowance cannot reuse an old generation. |
| AC3: exact node-only hosts | NodeProfile round-trip and registered common-directory resolution; 1–64 exact canonical public DNS hosts accepted per existing broker rules. Wildcards, suffix grants, URL, credentials, ports, paths, IPs, reserved canary and malformed/oversize lists rejected. Missing/unregistered repo grants nothing. Repository YAML, candidate edits/env and fork inputs cannot grant hosts or select helper. Preserve existing broker denial for unlisted redirect/CDN targets and credential tests; do not recreate transport implementation. |
| AC3: preparation/doctor and diagnostics | Extend existing workflow/validator tests for runtime selection, correct owner/base/policy propagation, unsupported backend preservation and no execution after failure. Doctor uses the same decision and explains missing capability/allowance without restoring or contacting public registries. Preserve node status consistency and repository-config rejection. Extend cache parser and executor fixtures to verify read-only consumption with run-local metadata and unchanged network denial. |
| AC3: format/current trusted policy/live evidence | Developer changed-file formatting and focused diagnostics below; coordinator current trusted required policy once on final candidate. Operator separately records installed-client restore/offline consumption evidence during PR review. Missing installed clients does not block implementation or fixture/CI acceptance. |

## Developer-owned focused evidence

## Correction-only classification regressions (AC2)

Add `TestSandboxRestorePreflightClassification` in existing `internal/sandbox/restore_test.go` and extend existing Linux/preparation fixtures in restore_linux_test.go and dependency_cache_test.go under the same TestSandboxRestore prefix. These are required assertions for the step 2a exception, not a replacement for unchanged acceptance coverage above:

- Nil, ordinary errors and lookalike error messages are not unavailable. Genuine missing helper/Bubblewrap and unavailable preflight restriction/control frames qualify only through CheckRestoreBoundary after teardown. Verify exact NETWORK/FILESYSTEM/BROKER/LISTENER/TRUST statuses and startup/control-framing paths without parsing diagnostics for authority. Preserve existing sanitized message assertions. Typed platform-denied listener setup can qualify; generic setup/I/O errors cannot. Invalid helper shape/build, registry policy, approved-source/root/snapshot errors, cancellation/deadline, timeout and broker policy errors remain fatal.
- Test all-branch classification with single wrappers, nested joins, reversed order, nil join children, capability-only joins, and capability joined with each discard/close/broker teardown/process-stop failure. Test an unknown leaf and a fatal leaf whose text says capability unavailable. Every fatal combination returns false; underlying causes remain discoverable with errors.Is/errors.As. An outer join of a CheckRestoreBoundary unavailable error and fatal cleanup also returns false. Never mark an aggregate unavailable merely because one child matches.
- Use small package-private classification/finalization helpers and existing fixtures to exercise deterministic combinations without launching real Bubblewrap. Verify actual preflight return classification follows deferred teardown and that finalization sees joined cleanup errors, rather than testing only marker constructors. Add only a narrow unexported failure seam if existing fixtures cannot inject the cleanup error; preserve production cleanup order and calls. Deterministic assertions must run even where real boundary tests skip.
- Raw internal capability markers and equivalent startup failures returned by Run never satisfy the exported predicate. Preparation retains host mounts and invokes no payload only for genuine preflight-only unavailable results. Policy/source/cleanup failures stop preparation; no publication or stale-generation reuse occurs. Every Run error, including launcher-start/restriction/payload/timeout/cleanup failure, stops preparation with no fallback, independent of error shape. Verify agent and validator propagation and doctor's matching unavailable-versus-fatal decision through the existing planned fixtures.
- Source review must confirm all tagged origins are narrow, no marker wraps a joined aggregate, no permissions/limits/runtime/helper changes occur, and no Run error callsite uses the fallback predicate. Review the demonstrated missing-bwrap/unsupported-platform propagation without widening any other restoreCommand errors.

Retain that skip honestly and preserve its adversarial assertions; deterministic joined-error tests supply the new classification evidence, not proof of real cleanup execution. ## Independent tester-owned review and reuse

Independently inspect the implementation and acceptance mapping, especially all-branch classification after final teardown, preflight-only marker provenance, unconditional Run failure propagation, trusted-base materialization, true runtime selection, helper origin, policy withdrawal, fallback phase, safefs publication/cleanup and read-only owner isolation. Compare exact argv and mounts with unchanged prerequisite contracts and existing adversarial tests. Confirm no protected edits, changed production limits/runtime manifest/exclusions, credential forwarding, network/socket/mount authority expansion or native/OCI enablement. Review successful and failed cache state assertions, not only return errors.

Reuse applicable passing developer commands against the same source. Repeat only for relevant source changes, observed failure or unresolved coverage concern; record the reason and smallest additional check. Add a targeted regression for an observed missing security case. Do not repeat all commands or run make check/full-suite/full-race merely because this is a separate role. Record evidence reuse, independent findings and remaining operator-only checks in validation handoff. Agent evidence remains advisory, not claim-bound validation or publication authority.

## Coordinator-owned required policy reference

After developer and tester finish, coordinator alone loads the approved-base policy and runs its complete current required checks once on the final candidate through the fenced validation workflow. SYSTEM_PROMPT.md's compiled policy currently lists fmt, build, lint, staticcheck, cli-smoke-security, filesystem-security, agent-security, sandbox-security, fork-security, core-regressions and changelog-regressions. This list is a reference, not an agent checklist; authoritative commands come from the approved base. Do not substitute the earlier make check/go test ./.../full-race campaign. Repeat only if relevant candidate changes or failures invalidate results. No agent subprocess requests credentials, stages approval or publishes.

On a host with installed clients, record versions, selected harness-tools Bubblewrap backend, approved base and node-approved exact hosts. Restore representative .NET/Maven/Gradle projects for both owners and demonstrate subsequent offline consumption from the isolated generation with corresponding host cache binds removed. Confirm immutable payload/run-local metadata separation, cross-repository/owner isolation, missing-capability doctor explanation and stop-on-started-failure behavior. Record Gradle in-process/daemon behavior and fixed-limit startup outcomes with existing exclusions/limits intact. Native Codex/OCI remain unchanged. These real installed-client checks are PR-review evidence, not implementation blockers; no new probe/performance campaign is requested.

## Developer report

# ISSUE-188 implementation

Implemented the corrected human-approved plan, including narrow step 2a. The earlier no-change stop is resolved. Read SYSTEM_PROMPT.md, WORKUNIT.md, PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md and APPROVED REVIEW.md before editing. No approval, staging, claim renewal, validation attestation or publication was attempted by this subprocess.

## Changes and acceptance evidence

- NodeProfile.restore_registries maps registered owner/repo names to dotnet/maven/gradle exact-host lists. Registered Git common-directory resolution supplies the policy; invalid selected entries persist as fatal policy errors even through the diagnostics-free loader. Missing/unregistered entries grant nothing. Existing profile serialization handles the added field without changing profile.go. Broker validation is reused through a thin wrapper. Repository configuration rejects the grant.
- Agent preparation selects the actual phase roles, shares native runtime selection with configured adapters, excludes custom runners and non-native isolation, and strips restore caches from native Codex consumption. Minimal engine/execute_plan call-site edits pass phase roles, preventing a configured but unused Bubblewrap role from enabling restore during a Codex phase. Validator selection excludes runner-isolated/host/OCI and native Codex checks.
- CheckRestoreBoundary finalizes classification after run and all its deferred teardown. Origin markers are private; Run never produces a completed-preflight marker. Every branch of wrappers/joins must qualify; aggregates hidden inside an origin marker are rejected. Typed listener permission/unsupported-operation errors qualify only through a single cause chain. Unknown I/O, source/policy errors, cancellation/deadline and fatal cleanup remain fatal. Internal deadline state is observed before the run's own deferred cancellation. A private afterCleanup test seam supplies deterministic final-close failures without replacing production cleanup calls. Diagnostics retain their existing strings.
- Restore adapters materialize bounded regular approved Git objects, reject unsafe tree entries and generated-settings collisions, discover sorted unique nested roots, and invoke fixed absolute installed clients. Candidate files and environment are not preparation inputs. Public feed layout uses the first allowed host; other exact hosts permit redirects/artifacts. Clean homes and client-owned cache paths preserve the existing proxy/trust environment.
- Publication uses owner/repository directories, exclusive private generations, safefs copying and atomic completed selectors. Identity includes approved bytes/base, adapter revision, installed launcher bytes and normalized host policy. Current allowance and preflight precede warm reuse. Root identity is rechecked. Existing filelock serializes competing publishers. Only NuGet packages, Maven repository contents and Gradle modules-2 payloads are imported; settings/home/trust/project outputs are excluded. Unsafe permissions, links, special files, oversize output, changed roots and payload errors fail preparation and discard unpublished output. Run errors propagate unconditionally; no Run path calls the fallback predicate.
- Successful ecosystems remove all matching host cache binds. Published lower directories mount read-only. Maven and Gradle use existing Bubblewrap discarded overlay mounts for run-local metadata; this supports the fixed older Gradle runtime without relying exclusively on newer GRADLE_RO_DEP_CACHE support. Unavailable/unconfigured restores retain host mounts. Shared-host opt-in and unrelated adapters remain intact.
- Doctor uses the same typed capability decision without restoring or contacting public registries. Node summaries describe conditional restore eligibility. Updated project and Claude/OpenCode/omp setup guides, clarified the native Codex exclusion, and added changes/unreleased/188.md (absent before editing).

Fixed permissions, resource flags, runtime manifest/exclusions, helper implementation and packaging are unchanged. No protected files or approved active inputs were edited. The broker change only exposes its existing exact-host validation.
